metadata.title: Andean crops nutrient composition dataset
metadata.description: Proximate composition, energy, selected minerals and vitamin C of Andean crops, with per-value provenance and verification status.
metadata.basis: All values are per 100 g edible portion of the food in the state described for each crop (for example dry seed, dried hypocotyl, fresh tuber or fresh fruit). Values are not comparable across these states without conversion.

verification_levels.verified: Checked against the primary source record by a curator.
verification_levels.corroborated: Matches the named source record as reproduced by at least one independent secondary copy; the primary record was not accessed.
verification_levels.unverified: Source not identified, or value not checked against any source.

methods.text: Values are expressed per 100 g edible portion of the food as described. Dry-matter values are calculated as value × 100 / (100 − water) and are shown only where water content is available. Per-energy values are calculated as value × 100 / energy and express nutrient density per 100 kcal.
Each record states whether the source food matches the crop directly or is a proxy (for example, a source that does not specify the species).

Energy is recalculated with general conversion factors of 4 kcal/g for protein and available carbohydrate, 9 kcal/g for fat and 2 kcal/g for dietary fibre, approximating available carbohydrate as total carbohydrate by difference minus dietary fibre. A difference of more than 10 % from the reported energy is flagged for review. The 10 % tolerance is a screening heuristic set for this dataset, not a published limit.

Where water and ash are reported, the sum of water, protein, fat, total carbohydrate and ash is expected to lie between 97 and 103 g/100 g. When carbohydrate is calculated by difference the sum equals 100 g by construction, so this check mainly detects transcription errors and values combined from different samples.

components.label: Energy
components.description: Metabolisable energy as reported by the source.

components.label: Protein
components.description: Total protein, conventionally calculated from total nitrogen; the nitrogen conversion factor is not recorded.

components.label: Fat, total
components.description: Total lipid. INFOODS distinguishes fat tagnames by analytical method; the method is not recorded here.

components.label: Carbohydrate, total (by difference)
components.description: Total carbohydrate calculated by difference; includes dietary fibre. It is not available carbohydrate.

components.label: Dietary fibre
components.description: Total dietary fibre for USDA-sourced values. For undocumented sources the method is unknown and the value may be crude fibre (INFOODS FIBC), which is not comparable with total dietary fibre.

components.label: Iron
components.description: Total iron; bioavailability is not represented.

components.label: Zinc
components.description: Total zinc; bioavailability is not represented.

components.label: Vitamin C
components.description: Total ascorbic acid as reported by the source; losses during storage, processing and cooking are not represented.

notes.text: Flavonoids, chiefly quercetin and kaempferol glycosides; total flavonoids in the quinoa and kañiwa samples studied ranged from 36.2 to 144.3 mg/100 g.
Bitter saponins are concentrated in the outer seed layers; grain is usually dehulled or polished and washed before use, and low-saponin ('sweet') cultivars are being developed.
Seed oil with linoleic acid as the main fatty acid and a high tocopherol content (reported jointly for quinoa and kañiwa).
